questions.q: What does `git push origin main` do?
options: Downloads the latest commits from GitHub
Sends your local commits on main to the origin remote
Creates a brand-new repository on GitHub
Deletes the main branch on GitHub
questions.explain: git push uploads commits that exist locally but not yet on the remote, to the named branch on the named remote.

questions.q: What does `git fetch` do that `git pull` does not?
options: It deletes uncommitted changes automatically
It downloads new commits from the remote without merging them into your working files
It pushes your local commits to the remote
It creates a new branch automatically
questions.explain: git fetch retrieves new commits and stores them locally, but stops short of merging — letting you inspect changes before deciding what to do with them.

questions.q: What is `git pull`, in terms of the other two commands this lesson covers?
options: A command with no relationship to fetch or push
git push followed immediately by git commit
git fetch followed immediately by git merge, run as one command
git fetch run twice in a row
questions.explain: git pull is fetch + merge combined — it grabs new commits and immediately merges them into your current branch.

questions.q: What does the `-u` flag do the first time you push a new local branch (`git push -u origin main`)?
options: It sets up a remembered pairing between the local branch and the remote branch, so future push/pull commands don't need the names spelled out
It undoes the last commit before pushing
It deletes the branch after pushing
It forces the push even if it would overwrite remote history
questions.explain: -u (--set-upstream) tells Git to remember which remote branch this local branch tracks, simplifying future push/pull commands.

questions.q: Why might you deliberately run `git fetch` instead of `git pull` when a teammate has pushed changes to a dbt model?
options: Because git fetch is required before every commit
To inspect what changed (e.g. with git log) before merging it into your own work in progress
Because git fetch permanently deletes the remote's version
Because git pull is not a real Git command
questions.explain: Fetching first lets you review incoming changes before merging, which git pull skips by merging immediately — useful when you don't want a surprise merge conflict mid-task.
